correctness.rationale: For forcing a=P sin θ, the positive near-identity ratio r solves r²−(1+a/y)r−a/y=0 with r(0)=1. The exact identity y'−y=4a+a(r−1)²/r, together with r=1+2a/y+O((a/y)²), gives the cubic term and no quadratic term. Intermediate squared speeds differ by O(|P|); the three sines sum to zero and their cubes give −3 sin(3θ)/4. After rescaling by the initial y, joint analyticity on a uniform neighborhood of P/y=0 gives a first angular derivative of the normalized remainder of order O((|P|/y)^4). At the grid phases the zero forcing is an identity and the other maps invert one another on the near-identity branch by swapping input and output in the implicit equation. The remainder thus vanishes on the grid, and distance to the grid is at most π|sin(3θ)|/6, proving relative control and sign. With c=−3P³sin(3θ), the return increments y³ by 3c+o(1). Monotonicity and continuity give increasing escape or finite descent past every fixed high cutoff; on descent, the steps from a fixed auxiliary level to the target are uniformly bounded, giving the stated hitting time. The angle has least period three. This verifies only the specified branch and high-energy domain.
residual_risks: Numerical checks are finite, not a proof of the uniform estimate. The implicit relation can have another positive root; the result only selects the branch near identity.
